361189.review_depth: source e-print read in full for the conjecture (Conj 050522f, Thm mainTheorem, Appendix A; arXiv:2312.10914 v3) + own exact exhaustive search beyond the authors' range
361189.summary: Conjecture verified for n=8 (first case beyond the source n<=7): with L_7=56 (source), all 87,956 deficient 8-path forests with l_1>=56 are impossibly burnable; the search closes at m=31 (no deficient forest for m>=31). Also computed L_8=68: no deficient 8-path forest with l_1>=68, exactly one with l_1=67, namely (67,67,67,67,102,102,102,102) at m=26 (impossibly burnable), so Question mainQuestion holds for n=8 and L_8=M_8+1, consistent with Conj 071222a (L_8<=96). Delta_8=54<L_7=56: the slack appears first at n=8 (deficient, not impossibly burnable: (53,53,53,53,53,53,82,84) at m=22; none with l_1>=54). n=9 with L_8=68: m=25..29 complete and m=30 extensions + first 10^6 balanced candidates, 37,861 deficient forests, all impossibly burnable; remainder stopped by CPU caps.
361189.method: Reduction lemma: if T in D(m) (deficient, parts>=L, order m^2) has largest part > 2m-2+L, removing 2m-1 from it gives a member of D(m-1). Hence D(m) is contained in Ext(D(m-1)) together with Balanced(m) (all parts in [L, 2m-2+L]), and each candidate is decided exactly by DFS over {1,3,...,2m-1} with exact-key failure memo and parity/count pruning. Validated against source: n=4 (47 deficient), n=5 (608), n=6 (5185), n=7 full table (178,1588,5460,9536,9572,1294,79,4,0) and the unique (45,45,45,45,72,74,74).
361189.coverage: scripts/burn.c, burn2.c, burn_driver.py; logs/burn-n*.log, logs/burn2-n*-L*-m*-s*.log; outputs/burn/*/state.json (intermediate D(m) binaries removed; reproducible).
361189.remaining: No counterexample; Delta_n appears to grow slower than L_{n-1}. A proof for all n remains open (source remarks the induction on L_{n-1} is doubtful).

353203.review_depth: source e-print read (uniqueness definition, Cor K_{2,t}(e), Prop p:K33, Conj; arXiv:2201.01798) + survey e-print (arXiv:2406.05509: Thm t:main TAR-iso => same X-sets after relabelling; still lists the conjecture as open) + own SAT computation and partial proof
353203.summary: By the published reduction (Bong-Carlson-Curtis-Haas-Hogben 2023, survey Thm t:main), uniqueness of PD-TAR(K_{s,t}) is equivalent to: K_{s,t} is the only graph without isolated vertices on A u B having exactly its power dominating sets. Encoded exactly as SAT (minimal PD sets via forcing chronologies; maximal non-PD sets via forts; E != E(K_{A,B})) and solved with cadical: UNSAT (uniqueness) for (s,t) in {(3,4),(3,5),(4,4),(4,5),(3,6),(4,6),(5,5),(3,7),(5,6),(3,8),(3,9),(4,7)}; new beyond the source are (3,6),(3,7),(3,8),(3,9),(4,6),(4,7),(5,5),(5,6). (3,3) is SAT only via relabelled K_{3,3} (all-pairs family is fully symmetric; source proves it). Controls (2,3),(2,4) SAT as the source predicts. Partial proof: blocker duality shows the minimal sets N[fort] are exactly B u {x,y} and A u {u,v}; if every minimal fort Psi_xy with N[Psi]=B u {x,y} is {x,y}, then H=K_{s,t} (proved).
353203.coverage: scripts/pdsat.py, pdsat_ablate.py, pdcheck.py; logs/pdsat-*.log, logs/abl-*.log (ablation: every constraint group is needed). CNFs removed (regenerable).
